notes:
- V1 CLOSED for the forms it cited. `--mirror`, `--delete`, `-d`, `--prune`, unambiguous abbreviations (`DANGEROUS_OPTIONS.some(o => o.startsWith(name))`, shell.ts 369-373) and `$'\x2d\x2dforce'` or octal or `\u` escapes (`decodeEscape`, 116-147) now give `force-push`. A push argument holding `$ ` `` ` `` `{ } * ? [ ] \` gives `unclear` (358, 382). Residual: B1 below.
- V2 CLOSED for the cited shapes. `<<<` is checked before `<<` (shell.ts 248-252) and is read as a redirect with a target word. `$((…<<…))` is covered by `scan.arithmetic`. `((…))` at the start of a command is skipped whole (211-221). Residual: B3 below. V4 (fail-open on stack overflow) is also CLOSED. `MAX_NESTING` of 64 sets `overflow`, which gives `unclear`, and hook.ts 239 turns an exception into `unclear`, not silence.
- B1 (validated, V1 class, a variant of the fixed path). `git push $'--force\0' origin main`, or `$'--force\x00'`. `decodeEscape` turns `\0` or `\x00` into U+0000 and keeps the rest of the word, so the arg is `--force\0`. `dangerous()` fails because `"--force".startsWith("--force\0")` is false, and `UNREADABLE` does not contain NUL, so the verdict is []. Bash truncates a `$'…'` string at NUL, so git receives `--force`. The same applies to `git $'commit\0' -m x` and to `+main`. Fix: treat a decoded NUL as unclear, or cut the word at it as bash does.
- B2 (validated, heredoc-delimiter class the brief asked about). The body of an unquoted heredoc is not data: bash runs `$(…)` and backticks in it. `readHeredoc` (46-70) never records whether the delimiter was quoted, and `skipHeredocs` (34-43) drops every body line. Command: `cat <<EOF` newline `$(git commit -m x)` newline `EOF`. It returns []. The same holds for `gh pr create --body-file - <<EOF … $(git push --force …) … EOF`, a very ordinary shape. Fix: for an unquoted delimiter, scan the body as if it were a double-quoted string, so substitutions in it are read.
- B3 (validated, V2 class). `<<` is read as a heredoc whenever `scan.arithmetic === 0`, but bash also uses it as a shift in three places the scanner does not count: the legacy `$[1<<2]`, `(( ))` not at the start of a command (after `if`, `while`, `elif`, `!`, `time`, whose words fill `words`), and the C-style `for ((i=1<<2; …))`. Command: `echo $[1<<2]` newline `git commit -m x`, or `if ((1<<2)); then :; fi` newline `git push --force`. The scanner opens a heredoc with delimiter `2]` or `2` and skips every later line until one equals it, so the second line is never scanned. Fix: do not open a heredoc when the `<<` has no delimiter-shaped word after it or sits inside any arithmetic context, and treat any heredoc whose terminator never arrives as unclear.
- B4 (validated, parser). `scanDouble` (80-82) keeps backslash-newline inside double quotes as the two characters `\\\n`, while bash deletes them. `git "com\<newline>mit" -m x # git commit` gives the subcommand `com\\\nmit`, which is not `commit`, so the verdict is []. `git "pu\<newline>sh" --force origin push` hides a force push the same way. The `if` rule is satisfied by a later literal word or a comment. Fix: drop `\` plus newline in `scanDouble`.
- B5 (validated). `((` at the start of a command is skipped whole by paren counting (211-221), but arithmetic runs command substitutions. Command: `(( $(git commit -m x; echo 1) ))`. The scanner never sees the inner `git commit`. Fix: scan the `$(` and backtick contents inside the skipped text, or treat the construct as unclear.
- Non-blocking, still open from the first review or acknowledged by the hook comment at hook.ts 159-163. (a) Nested backticks: ``echo `echo \`git commit -m x\```. (b) Wrappers not in `WRAPPERS`: `eval 'git commit -m x'`, `setsid`, `stdbuf`, `ionice`, `flock`, `find -exec`, `ssh`, `env -S 'git commit'`, `fish -c`, and a shell reading its script from a heredoc or pipe (`bash <<'EOF'`, `echo 'git commit -m x' | sh`). (c) Dynamic subcommand or git alias: `p=push; git $p -f origin main # git push`, `git -c alias.pf='push -f' pf origin main`, `git -c remote.origin.push=+HEAD push origin`, `git --config-env foo=BAR commit`. The last also shows that `--config-env` and `--attr-source` are missing from `VALUE_OPTIONS`, so the subcommand is misread. The hook applies the deny-the-unknown rule to push arguments but not to the subcommand or to the global options. Applying it there would close most of (c) and the variable cases at once. These are a design limit as far as the docs go, but `docs/hooks.md` lists only the covered wrappers and should state the rest.
- Non-blocking, commit-msg (hook.ts 249-290, new in this repair). Everything after a line equal to `<comment> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------` is cut off before the attribution clean and the phrase check, and written back unchanged. A hand-built message containing that line followed by `Co-Authored-By: Claude …` or text about the user keeps it in the commit. `git -c core.commentString=X commit` reaches the hook through `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, so every line starting with `X` is also skipped. Only a `git commit` that got past the redirect is affected, and `vcs commit` checks the full text. The V5 `#`-line case also remains.
- Unverified (S1): whether the `Bash(*git*commit*)` and `Bash(*git*push*)` `if` globs match a multi-line command. B2 and B3 need a newline. The documented probe on Claude Code 2.1.310 covers `&&` lists and subshells only. If a newline stops the match, the hook never runs for those commands, which is a separate bypass.
- Sound, no finding: the `unclear` verdict and `REDIRECTS` text; hook.ts failure handling (every exception becomes a deny and no longer a silent pass); the `workflowRefusal` call (default path stays 'no decision', and only a `script`/`args` input reaches it); `ownerOf` in report.ts (a stricter support test, no new sink); instruction and docs text (no security sink); `state/local.ts` (comment-only change). The `shell.test.ts` cases cover the earlier V1 and V2 examples, but none of B1 to B5.
- Scope: I read only the shell.ts and hook.ts files in /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-fix-cli-and-vcs, plus the first 881 lines of pr6-repair.diff and then lines 1086-1281, which hold the rest of the shell.ts diff and the tests; I did not open the diff lines 882-1085. `workflow-check.ts` is out of scope. The tree is another worker's worktree and may have been changing. The independence rule holds: I took no part in the repair.
